_comment: EXT-63 SMOKE, arm 3 — arm 2 plus ONE key: the a00 Kaula prior tightened from
sigma 30 TECU to 5 TECU.  This is a MECHANISM TEST, not a proposed fix.
WHAT ARM 2 MEASURED.  With sbasis_complete armed the datum closed (0 gate withholds,
20/20 epochs SOLVED), but the SH health gate withheld 19 of 20 emissions and never
released ('STILL ENGAGED at run end — the era outlived the data').  The a00 trajectory
from network_vtec_sh_health.csv:
ep 1  a00 = +12.77 TECU   sigma 3.94
ep 2  a00 = -49.98        sigma 2.40    <- SBC released its epoch-1 gauge row here
The estimate walks monotonically away from the DOY-129 field truth (30-33 TECU) while
its FORMAL SIGMA COLLAPSES — confident and wrong.  That is the diagonal-carry lock-in
signature, riding a direction that has no datum.
THE DIAGNOSIS.  EXT-CB removes the satellite code-bias columns and, with them, the
per-(constellation,signal) SUM-TO-ZERO code-bias gauge.  That gauge was silently doing
double duty: it also anchored the RECEIVER-DCB common mode, which trades one-for-one
against the global ionosphere LEVEL (Odijk's i~ = i + d_r,GF - d^s,GF — hand d^s to the
product and the d_r half is left ungauged).  The rx DCB is a LOCAL, Schur-eliminated
state, so in the shared border the free direction shows up spread across the phase-bias
and SH columns — matching the sbc_engage attribution, whose top span was only 0.12
(PB:G06:L2X), i.e. a diffuse direction with no dominant column, NOT a per-satellite one.
Corroborating: the rx-CB carry withheld 869 of 1158 folds on its 10-sigma innovation
gate, and the rxcb prior-residual contingency is raw_flat-above 24 of 24 (100%) — the
receiver code-bias estimates jump while the raw observables are provably FLAT.
WHAT THIS ARM DECIDES.  a00's Kaula prior (15 +- 30 TECU) is currently the ONLY thing
resisting that direction, and 1/30^2 leaves it 1.7x short of the rank-gate cutoff.  At
sigma 5 the information rises 36x (eigenvalue ~1.3e-4 -> ~4.8e-3, ~21x above cutoff).
Two outcomes, both informative, and the prior MEAN is deliberately left at its wrong-ish
15 TECU so the test is not tuned to the answer:
a00 settles near 25-35 TECU (i.e. it PULLS AWAY from the 15 TECU prior mean toward the
true field): the data DOES determine the level; the prior only had to be strong enough
to keep the solve out of the runaway basin.  Then the honest fix is a real receiver-DCB
datum (the standard IGS zero-mean-over-receivers convention that replaces the
satellite-DCB zero-mean we gave away), and this prior is a crutch.
a00 pins at ~15 TECU (sits on the prior mean): the data does NOT determine the level at
all and the prior IS the entire datum.  That is the more serious reading, and it says
the same about the W6 arms — where the level is being set by the satellite code-bias
datum CONVENTION rather than by the observations.
Either way this is a DIAGNOSTIC arm.  Do not inherit it into a science lineage.
